prompts.bugbear:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset: game pixel sprite sheet edit. Image 1 is the sheet to redraw; image 2 and 3 are supporting game art STYLE references only. Redraw the entire first sheet with a SUBSTANTIALLY MORE TOP-DOWN camera: viewer high above the creature looking down approximately 45 degrees from the south. Show a broad top-of-head/crown, upper surfaces of shoulders and upper back. Those overhead planes dominate the upper TWO THIRDS of each body silhouette. Faces, chest and legs are strongly vertically foreshortened into lower third. Side-facing rows must visibly show the TOP plane of head and shoulders/back, not an eye-level side profile. Do not merely add shading or move eyes to previous frontal poses; change anatomy projection across ALL 32 frames. Keep the identity, colors and attack weapon/actions of first image. Chunky simple low-resolution game pixel style of supporting refs, dark single-pixel outlines, very few flat shaded color clusters, no noisy texture. EXACT 8 equal columns by 4 equal rows, landscape 2:1 sheet, no labels/gridlines. Each equal cell logically 32x32. ROW 1 north/up-screen away from camera (back of head/back); ROW2 east/right; ROW3 south/down-screen facing camera with visible crown foreshortened face; ROW4 west/left. First four columns distinct WALK phases alternating feet/arms; last four attack anticipation, windup, impact, recovery. Same scale, foot anchor and center each cell, all body and entire weapons contained inside individual cells with transparent margins. Keep attacks visibly directed toward the row direction. Top-down square grid, NOT isometric, NO diamonds. Transparent background actual alpha, no ground shadows/props, no gradients or antialiasing.
Specific target: bugbear. Preserve its original design and palette.

prompts.giant-bear: Use case: style-transfer. Edit target is image1 existing enemy spritesheet. Images2 and3 are STYLE REFERENCES for game pixel art, not layout. Redraw image1 with a SUBSTANTIALLY more overhead viewpoint, camera above and south looking downward ~45 degrees (emphasize top surfaces, elevated camera, not eye-level), for a square-grid top-down RPG. Retain character identity/colors. Do not copy the original front-facing proportions. Dominant visible head-crown, top shoulders, upper back; compress face/chest/legs beneath them. Side facings must show broad top surfaces of backs, not flat side-on profile. No isometric diamond-grid. Crisp chunky flat limited-palette pixel art matching the supplied monster and brute references, broad clusters, no fine texture/noisy detailed illustration. Exactly EIGHT columns and FOUR rows, 32 distinct separated frames on true transparent background. Layout row1 north/back screen-up, row2 east/right, row3 south/toward viewer screen-down, row4 west/left. Each row columns1-4 walk/slither cycle; columns5-8 attack anticipation, windup, strike, recovery. All frames designed as native32x32 squares, final sheet256x128; if generated larger preserve exact2:1 sheet and uniform4x8 grid for nearest-neighbor reduction. Each sprite completely inside own square with 2px padding at native size. All tails/weapons inside frame. Consistent scale/center/feet through row. No text, labels, grid lines, scenery or shadows. Giant brown bear with cream muzzle and claws. Major correction: walk on all fours with broad rounded back filling most of silhouette, top of bear skull plainly visible, muzzle low at front edge, far paws largely hidden by back. In right/left rows show an overhead oblique quadruped, back is a broad oval and legs are short projections. No tall standing chest attack; use low paw swipe and forward bite/lunge with top of back still dominant. Keep direction obvious.
